_doc: Dress sheets for batch p06 (design/world/depth/art/_brief-portraits.md): five sects with no sheet in dress.json. Cultivators dress well: plain never ragged.
phuong_minh: Phượng Minh Cung, the palace of the phoenix's call: robes cut like a court musician's, with a wide crossed collar, long straight sleeves and a high sash. Outer disciples wear fine undyed hemp, pale and clean, tied with a single red cord at the waist. Inner disciples wear vermilion silk, a clear orange-red, with a darker red sash. Elders keep the vermilion and add narrow coloured bands along the hem, one band for each of the five marks they have lit, in the order gold, white, green, black, red; the head wears all five. Hair is pinned up with a slim red-lacquer or wutong-wood pin, and many carry a long red tail-feather tucked behind the ear. They carry fans, never swords: a folding fan of red-dyed feathers or silk, held at the chest or tucked in the sash. Small painted emblems of a bird in flight may sit on a fan, never text.
le_hoa: Lê Hoa Am, the hermitage of the pear blossom, in two robes. White nuns shave their heads smooth and wear undyed white wool-silk, a high crossed collar, wide sleeves and a plain white sash, with a string of pale pear-wood beads at the neck or wrist; an abbess adds a sheer white veil-robe over the shoulders. Grey sisters keep their hair, bound up in a plain knot or a grey cloth, and wear well-fitted dove-grey wool, a quilted jacket in the cold, a dark sash and boots; they carry a straight sword in a plain scabbard. No gold, no colour; the only ornament is a single pale pear-wood bead or a small white pear-blossom of carved bone.
truc_thuc: Trúc Thực Viên, the garden of the bamboo seed: undyed bamboo-fibre cloth, a pale straw-beige with a fine woven grain, cut as a plain crossed-collar jacket and trousers or a knee-length robe, clean and well fitted; wide conical straw hats of split bamboo, worn or hung at the back on a cord; and mud on the boots to the knee, honest work-mud, not tatters. Rank shows in the tool carried on the belt or in the hand: a short curved seed knife for outer hands, a small brass sluice key for the inner gate, a squat red-clay censer for the head alone. Green bamboo-leaf ties or a sprig of bamboo are the only decoration.
vu_an: Vụ Ẩn Môn, the gate hidden in mist: grey-green oiled cloaks, long and hooded or caped to the knee, dull and damp-sheened; wide round bamboo hats with a cord under the chin; under the cloak a plain dark-grey tunic and sash, and straw sandals or wrapped boots. On the road every guard carries a lantern hung from a pole or a cord, small, with a frosted paper or horn shade; lanterns outrank decoration. No badges and no names worn; a road guard gives none. The captain's and elders' cloaks are the same cloth, only better kept.
tuan_tung: Tuần Tùng Đường, the hall of the pine wardens: wolfskin and grey wool, well cut and well worn. Outer wardens wear a grey wool coat with a strip of wolfskin sewn along the collar. Inner wardens add a wolfskin half-cape over the left shoulder. Elders wear a full wolfskin mantle over the grey wool. Everyone carries a bone or wooden whistle on a cord at the neck, and a staff or a short bow; fur boots and leather wrist guards. Dead wardens are remembered by a green pine needle worn at the collar. Cloth is thick, clean and dense, made for pine-forest cold.
